issue_context.title: Bug: ComboBox list shift to the right when clicked on
issue_context.body:
### Description

When clicking on a ComboBox list (list of selectable items) in Settings, the list moves away from under the cursor.

https://github.com/files-community/Files/assets/87632612/f9ab3841-c470-4430-a10c-33a00bfc5cb2



### Steps To Reproduce

1. Open Settings
2. Click on any ComboBox 
3. List moves to the right and is not at the same location as it was before.

### Requirements

Would be better if the list stays under the mouse cursor on being clicked.

### Files Version

Latest dev build (3.2.7.0)

### Windows Version

22631.3296

### Log File

[debug.log](https://github.com/files-community/Files/files/14611969/debug.log)
comments: I have found that setting a fixed `Width` or `MinWidth` for the `ComboBox` -es can solve this issue. Let me know if you guys think it is a viable option, and I'll make a PR for it.
Thanks for the report, I've added this to the project board. Please wait until the status is `Ready to build` on the right sidebar of this issue before opening a PR.

> I have found that setting a fixed `Width` or `MinWidth` for the `ComboBox` -es can solve this issue. Let me know if you guys think it is a viable option, and I'll make a PR for it.

We can set a MinWidth but we should avoid setting a fixed width because some languages or strings are longer.
Yup I figured that out. So I can start working on this, now that its in "Ready to build" right?
Yes, thank you! It might even be worth creating a custom resource dictionary for the ComboBox controls in settings so that we don't have to manually set this on every single instance.
This should be done by WinUI. I'll make a ticket for this in the repo and wait for a response.
Please thumb up and/or comment on the issue...

review_comments: We should not be using magic numbers here but a) not have them at all or b) look them up using resources

I thought the same thing but that's complicated because some of them use Thickness not Double.
We could do like this(at least should add comments) I guess.
If we add comments I guess it's fine, however if we restyle the controls one would also need to think about these numbers.

I would say this comment is not entirely correct. There are definitely cases where one wouldn't need this extension. The comment should probably indicate that in fact this extension is setting min width
We use this for ComboBoxes in Settings, which are aligned Right position. When there's no MinWidth popup opens at ugly position, swapping to the right.
What you describe is what bug this fixes, the symptom you are adressing. The extension however only sets the min width and the comment should explain exactly that in my opinion.
Why do these two methods not use the exact same code to set min width?
I think I can remove one of them. One of which didn't get fired on loaded.
